evals.name: create-board-with-milestones
evals.prompt: create a project for the Q4 billing migration (we're moving off Stripe Billing onto our own invoicing service, repo is at /Users/amit/workspaces/billing) with milestones and track progress
evals.expected_output: Checks project_list for an existing billing project, then project_create with a name, a description written as standing instructions, a working_directory attachment pointing at /Users/amit/workspaces/billing, and a deliberate run config (asked about or looked up via model_list rather than assumed). Milestones are modelled as parent issues with sub_issues via project_update, not invented as a milestone field.
assertions: Calls project_list before creating, to avoid a duplicate board
Calls project_create with name and a run config containing provider_id and model_id
Creates milestones as parent issues with sub_issues rather than inventing a milestone field
Does not call project_run (the user asked to plan, not execute)

evals.name: progress-report-across-pages
evals.prompt: where are we on the billing migration board? how much is actually done and what's blocked
evals.expected_output: project_list to resolve the id, then project_get. Because the answer is a count, it reads every page (and notes when the default_filter hid issues) rather than counting the first page. Reports grouped by status/milestone with blockers named, using titles rather than ids.
assertions: Resolves the project id with project_list rather than guessing
Reads the full board (pages with the cursor, or passes an explicit filter) rather than counting one page
Mentions the default_filter or explicitly widens it when the count could be incomplete
Names blocked issues and what blocks them
Reports by issue title, not by raw issue id

evals.name: close-and-sequence-work
evals.prompt: the invoice PDF renderer is done — mark it complete. also the dunning emails task can't start until the invoice API ships, can you wire that up
evals.expected_output: project_get first to read the real status ids and issue ids, then a single atomic project_update batch containing update_issue (status -> a complete-category status read from the board) and set_blocked_by on the dunning issue naming the invoice API issue. Uses set_blocked_by rather than reparenting, and does not remove_issue.
assertions: Calls project_get to read real status ids and issue ids before mutating
Uses update_issue with a complete-category status rather than remove_issue
Expresses the dependency with set_blocked_by, not by nesting as a sub-issue
Groups both changes into one project_update batch
Does not invent status ids such as 'done' without reading them from the board
